t: LeetCode 2158 — Amount of New Area Painted Each Day
o: Each day i paints the half-open stretch [start_i, end_i) of a number line, but already-painted spots are skipped, and worklog[i] records only the newly covered length. In Example 1 we paint [1,4), then [4,7), and finally only [7,8) of the requested [5,8) — answers 3, 3, 1. Example 2 reorders the requests and still reports 3, 3, 1, showing overlaps come from history rather than ordering tricks. Example 3 demonstrates a day can add nothing at all when its range was fully covered. Coordinates stay below 5*10^4 while there may be 10^5 days, so repainting unit-by-unit every day can degenerate to billions of operations; maintaining the painted region as a merged, sorted structure scales gracefully.
k: Painted territory only grows, so it is invariantly a sorted union of disjoint intervals.
New area on a day = requested length minus the total intersection with currently stored intervals.
Each interval is inserted once and absorbed at most once, so erasure work amortizes away on top of the per-day binary search.

a.i: Model the number line as one boolean cell per unit segment and literally paint: cells already marked are skipped, freshly marked ones count toward the day. Correct by construction and trivial to reason about, but a single day can sweep up to 5*10^4 cells, so dense inputs drive this toward ~5*10^9 cell visits.
s: Allocate a boolean cell for every unit segment below the maximum end coordinate.
Per day, walk every cell in [start, end).
Unpainted cells become painted and increment the counter; append it to the worklog.
a.t: O(sum of interval lengths) — up to ~5*10^9 unit-cell visits on dense inputs
a.sp: O(L) — one flag per unit segment, L <= 5*10^4

a.n: Approach 2: Sorted disjoint intervals with merging (optimal)
a.i: Keep the painted region as disjoint intervals sorted by start — parallel arrays with binary search, or a map/TreeMap keyed by start. For a request [s, e): locate the first interval that can overlap, walk right while intervals begin before e, charging their intersection with the FIXED query range, and expand the union hull. Erase the absorbed intervals, insert the hull, and report (e - s) minus the charged overlap. Every stored interval is created once and destroyed at most once, so maintenance amortizes beautifully.
s: Binary-search for the first stored interval whose end is >= s.
Walk right while interval.start < e, accumulating overlap with the fixed [s0, e0).
Expand the merged hull to cover all absorbed intervals.
Remove absorbed intervals, insert the hull in their place, and append (e0 - s0) - covered.

c.python:
from bisect import bisect_left

class Solution:
    def amountPainted(self, paint: List[List[int]]) -> List[int]:
        starts, ends, res = [], [], []
        for s0, e0 in paint:
            covered = 0
            i = bisect_left(ends, s0)
            j = i
            while j < len(starts) and starts[j] < e0:
                covered += min(e0, ends[j]) - max(s0, starts[j])
                j += 1
            ns, ne = s0, e0
            if j > i:
                ns = min(ns, starts[i])
                ne = max(ne, ends[j - 1])
            starts[i:j] = [ns]
            ends[i:j] = [ne]
            res.append(e0 - s0 - covered)
        return res

a.t: O(n log n) — one binary search per day; each stored interval is erased at most once (splice-based implementations add copying overhead in adversarial orders)

w: State the invariant — painted area is always a sorted union of disjoint intervals — before coding; interviewers reward the amortization argument that each stored interval dies once. Watch for: touching-but-not-overlapping ranges ([1,4) then [4,7) contribute zero overlap, though merging them harmlessly is fine), days fully covered by history answering 0, and consistent half-open semantics. In JavaScript, sorted-array splicing is fast on real tests but degrades toward O(n^2) on adversarial orders; std::map / TreeMap or a segment tree with range-assign lazy (guaranteed O(n log C)) removes the caveat. Follow-ups: interleave queries with paintings, or track weighted area.
